question: Toronto Mayoral Election Winner
resolution_criteria:
The 2026 Toronto mayoral election is currently scheduled to be held on October 26, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who becomes the next mayor of Toronto as a result of this election.

Temporary, interim, or placeholder mayors appointed before the election will not be considered.

If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting; however, if there is any ambiguity in the results, this market will resolve according to official information from Toronto.

"Other" means any option not listed here.
research:
I limited this to information published on or before 2026-10-10. Some of my search results included later polls and reporting, and I left all of that out.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on a consensus of credible reporting, with official City of Toronto results as the fallback if anything is unclear. The question gives no URL, so I did not fetch an official results page. Polling day is 2026-10-26.
- 2026-08-21: Nominations closed at 2 p.m. 55 candidates filed, two withdrew, and 53 ran for mayor. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Toronto_mayoral_election)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. In practice it is a two-way race between incumbent Olivia Chow and Brad Bradford.
- Of the other listed options, John Tory, Ana Bailão, Michael Ford, Anthony Furey and Marco Mendicino are not on the nominated candidate list. Some of them appeared only in pre-campaign polls. That means they are effectively out, and only Chow, Bradford and "Other" remain realistic. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Toronto_mayoral_election)
- 2026-10-06: Chris Alexander, the third-place candidate, dropped out as advance voting opened. He endorsed no one, and his name stays on the ballot because he quit after the withdrawal deadline. [CP24](https://cp24.com/gta-elections-2026/2026/10/06/chris-alexander-drops-out-of-race-to-become-torontos-next-mayor/), [Ground News](https://ground.news/article/chris-alexander-drops-out-of-toronto-mayors-race), [Western Standard](https://www.westernstandard.news/news/chris-alexander-quits-toronto-mayoral-race-as-advance-polls-open/77615)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
Polls are shown as Chow vs. Bradford. Field dates come from the Wikipedia table. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Toronto_mayoral_election)
- 2026-10-08/09: Liaison Strategies has Chow at 51% and Bradford at 46%.
- 2026-10-06/07: Mainstreet has Chow at 47% and Bradford at 44%, with 9% other or undecided.
- 2026-10-06: Scope Research (online, 3,100 respondents) has Chow at 51% and Bradford at 47%.
- 2026-10-06: Forum Research has Chow at 46% and Bradford at 42%, with 12% other or undecided. [NOW Toronto](https://nowtoronto.com/news/chow-leads-bradford-by-four-points-chris-alexander-exits-race-forum-research-poll/)
- 2026-10-03/04: Liaison Strategies has Chow 48%, Bradford 40%, Alexander 9%.
- 2026-09-30 to 10-04: Nanos for CTV/CP24 has Chow 52%, Bradford 43%, Alexander 4%. CTV described this as Chow leading by nearly 10 points. [CTV](https://www.ctvnews.ca/toronto/article/exclusive-poll-olivia-chow-leads-brad-bradford-by-nearly-10-points-chris-alexander-a-distant-third/)
- September: Chow led every poll by 7 to 23 points. The largest lead was Ipsos (Sep 4-8, decided voters) at 54% to 31%. The others mostly ranged from 45% to 51% for Chow and 34% to 40% for Bradford.
- The trend is clear: since Alexander left, Bradford has consolidated the centre-right vote, and Chow's lead has shrunk from roughly 8 to 10 points to about 3 to 5. Chow has stayed at or above about 46% in every poll.
- Endorsements:
  - Bradford: several Liberal MPs, Erin O'Toole, Lisa Raitt and ABC Toronto.
  - Chow: NDP figures, Kathleen Wynne, Bob Rae, Nate Erskine-Smith and major unions. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Toronto_mayoral_election)

## 4. Base rates
- Since amalgamation, every incumbent mayor of Toronto who ran again has won:
  - Lastman in 2000
  - Miller in 2006
  - Tory in 2018 and 2022
- The only post-amalgamation incumbent who lost was Rob Ford, and he did not run again in 2014. This comes from my own background knowledge; I did not look up a source for it in this session.
- Chow herself won the 2023 by-election with about 37% against a split field.
- A 3 to 5 point lead with about two weeks left is inside the typical polling error for municipal races. Municipal polls, which are often IVR (automated phone) polls, have historically missed by several points.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-09-02: Prediction Hunt said Chow was polling at 47% while markets priced her at 86%. [Prediction Hunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/news/chow-polls-at-47-but-markets-price-her-at-86-sep-02-2026)
- 2026-08-30: Prediction Hunt reported Chow's win probability had fallen 10 points despite an 8-point poll lead. [Prediction Hunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/news/chow-s-win-probability-drops-10-points-aug-30-2026)
- 2026-10-04: A tracker of the Polymarket market showed Chow at 88%. [Predscope](https://predscope.com/event/toronto-mayoral-election-winner-545)
- About 2026-10-10: A CryptoSlate mirror of the Polymarket market showed Chow at 71.5% and Bradford at 29.5%. That points to a sharp drop for Chow after Alexander left. These are third-party mirrors, so the numbers may be stale. [CryptoSlate](https://cryptoslate.com/predictions/market/who-will-win-the-2026-toronto-mayoral-election/), [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/toronto-mayoral-election-winner-545)
- I found no Kalshi or Manifold prices, and no expert seat-model style forecasts, published before 2026-10-10.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Advance voting has been under way since 2026-10-06.
- More polls are coming from Nanos, Liaison, Mainstreet, Pollara and Forum. The key question is whether Alexander's former 6 to 10% keeps moving to Bradford.
- Candidate debates and late endorsements are still ahead.
- Alexander's name stays on the ballot, so he may still draw a small number of votes.
- Polling day is 2026-10-26. The City usually reports unofficial results that night, and if the result is clear, credible reporting should settle the question well before the 2027-06-30 deadline.
